title: Stage endpoint contrasts
result: Observed/withheld endpoint contrasts differed through the saved encoder stages.
lesson: The support-associated contrast was selective; stage curves alone do not identify its cause.

title: Stage-contrast review
result: Located changes across embedding, blocks and final normalization in the same archive.
lesson: A review of D01 is not an independent replication.

title: Changed token versus CLS
result: Raw source-token identity separation persisted while CLS transfer differed by support.
lesson: Input information presence does not ensure it reaches the decision representation.

title: Exact first-attention decomposition
result: Recomputed first-attention value, weight and interaction terms for discovery cases.
lesson: The support-associated write could be decomposed; accounting is not unique causal attribution.

title: Attention-term review
result: Aggregated D03 terms and cancellations within models.
lesson: Do not count averaged term descriptions as a second causal discovery.

title: Symbol/normalization/projection separation
result: Compared all15 identity pairs through pre-attention transforms in permitted models.
lesson: Projection gain and direction matter beyond raw embedding distance.

title: A/B projection review
result: Summarized hole versus opposite-clique gains on D04.
lesson: Same-checkpoint comparisons remain exploratory.

title: C/D projection countercheck
result: Extended the gain description to non-A/B support structures.
lesson: An A/B pattern should not be called a universal support law.

title: False-twin versus distinguishing neighborhoods
result: Related learned contrasts to available graph-neighborhood distinctions.
lesson: Contextual distinguishability was a candidate explanation, not a proven necessity.

title: Degree explanation audit
result: Examined whether simple degree explained the contrast pattern.
lesson: No single graph statistic was isolated by these descriptive comparisons.

title: Asymmetric graph E
result: Defined a graph adding contextual identity distinctions.
lesson: A graph design can create a separating training comparison but is not a result.

title: Train graph E
result: E could preserve focal identity distinctions and held-out transfer where A compressed them.
lesson: Changing comparison context can change acquisition; later tied-E counterexample limits necessity.

title: A versus E comparison
result: A/E learned contrasts and transfer differed.
lesson: The contrast identifies a graph-package effect, not its unique causal feature.

title: Initialization versus final state
result: Compared initial and final contrast geometry.
lesson: Final differences cannot simply be assumed to preexist learning; no general acquisition law follows.

title: Exact training exposure
result: Enumerated the supervised/foil exposure differences between conditions.
lesson: Support comparisons require auditing actual episodes, not only graph names.

title: Graph E seed extension
result: Additional discovery seeds evaluated E's transfer behavior.
lesson: The initial E result was not the only observed initialization; still not protected confirmation.

title: Depth of contrast development
result: Tracked where the A/E contrast emerged across depth.
lesson: Depth localization is descriptive without selective operation interventions.

title: Changed token and CLS
result: Identity-bearing token and CLS contrast profiles differed.
lesson: A single readout token is not the full computational state.

title: Shared-scene support comparison
result: Compared permitted models on shared rendered scenes.
lesson: Shared inputs reduce a rendering confound but not training-package confounds.

title: Training-context signature
result: Characterized context support associated with contrasting acquisition.
lesson: Context statistics are candidate predictors, not identified mechanisms.

title: Matched E seed1701
result: Added a matched-initialization E comparison.
lesson: Initialization matching sharpens the training-condition contrast within this synthetic system.

title: Changed-token patches
result: Intervened on the changed identity-bearing token path.
lesson: Local causal influence can be tested; it need not imply a reusable symbolic operator.

title: Unchanged-token relays
result: Examined unchanged tokens as routes carrying a changed identity effect.
lesson: Effects can propagate through tokens whose surface identity did not change.

title: Candidate-side contrasts
result: Extended the contrast description to candidate encoders.
lesson: The query side alone cannot characterize compatibility decisions.

title: Exact shared-scene comparison
result: Tightened matching of rendered scenes between models.
lesson: Controls improve attribution to learning conditions, not to a unique internal cause.

title: Visual co-occurrence audit
result: Identities can co-occur as endpoint and distractor; the broad never-co-occur claim was false.
lesson: Supervised relation withholding is not visual identity co-occurrence withholding.

title: Discovery seed summary
result: Consolidated the accumulated A/E evidence across permitted starts.
lesson: Summarizing shared models does not create independent confirmation.

title: Enumerate constrained six-vertex graphs
result: 455 omit-three-edge graphs left only two focal classes under the constraints.
lesson: The proposed rich factorial was unavailable in that tiny graph space.

title: Comparison-rich F
result: Designed choice-foil modifications intended to preserve distinctions.
lesson: Later exposure audit was necessary: F also changed positive frequencies.

title: Train comparison-rich F
result: F gave strong held-out transfer across the focal identities.
lesson: A changed training comparison package can rescue synthetic transfer.

title: Frequency control G
result: Designed an overall-frequency comparator for F.
lesson: Frequency matching needs be explicit rather than assumed.

title: Train frequency control G
result: G held-out about.587 versus F.982.
lesson: The tested frequency change did not reproduce F's rescue.

title: F/G developmental contrasts
result: F amplified identity separation while G compressed it from a shared initialization.
lesson: The training condition altered acquisition dynamics; a curve is not a general law.

title: Comparison connectivity/resistance
result: Effective resistance/connectivity did not predict the A/E difference reliably.
lesson: A plausible graph scalar failed as a sufficient explanatory law.

title: Cross-task fitted solutions
result: Separated F solution fit A; collapsed A solution failed F.
lesson: A's loss permitted separated solutions; collapse was not mathematically forced by support.

title: A/F training task switch
result: Changed the ongoing training task between A and F.
lesson: Training history and current comparisons can be causally separated in this model.

title: Task-switch developmental review
result: A→F restored contrast; F→A only partly eroded it.
lesson: Acquisition exhibited path dependence rather than a unique endpoint from support alone.

title: A-loss parameter interpolation
result: Constructed interpolation paths with low A task loss.
lesson: Very different transfer behavior can coexist with similar familiar loss.

title: Redirection along interpolation
result: Unsupported-role redirection changed along the low-loss path.
lesson: Familiar task fit alone does not identify the transfer computation.

title: Identity merger across tasks
result: Merger raised F loss about.006→.091, with little A/G cost and small E cost.
lesson: F made the tested distinction more behaviorally consequential.

title: Extended F→A training
result: Continued A training after F acquisition.
lesson: A task switch can test whether the acquired distinction is rapidly lost.

title: Long withdrawal readout
result: After8k A updates source/target readout.955/.721 and redirection1/.922 persisted.
lesson: Strong path dependence survives extended withdrawal in this selected system.

title: Train identity-tied E
result: E could fit familiar data with tied focal identities.
lesson: Distinct contextual neighborhoods did not force separate identity representations.

title: Tied-E training readout
result: Intermediate evaluation of the same tied-E acquisition.
lesson: Not an additional training experiment or independent confirmation.

title: Tied versus untied E
result: Familiar S/R near1 for both; held tied.651 versus untied.975.
lesson: Familiar success and asymmetric context do not imply transferable separation.

title: Source-frequency H
result: Defined a source-frequency-matched control.
lesson: A marginal-frequency hypothesis can be tested separately from the full comparison package.

title: Train H
result: Held-out about.573, below the comparison-rich rescue.
lesson: Matching the tested source-family frequency did not reproduce F.

title: H developmental analysis
result: H contrasts compressed during training.
lesson: Source-frequency exposure alone did not preserve the tested distinction.

title: Tied-E release versus retention
result: Continued matched training with identity tying released or retained.
lesson: Releasing a constraint allows a direct acquisition comparison.

title: Release developmental readout
result: Released contrasts.655/.809, held.914; retained contrasts zero, held.671.
lesson: Acquiring identity separation improved transfer under E, without proving a universal mediator.

title: Tied/untied E loss
result: Losses.00518 versus.00683 were both small.
lesson: The distinction had a soft preference rather than being necessary for familiar success.

title: One-step identity gradient
result: A gradient norm.00662 exceeded E.00310 despite poorer later A transfer.
lesson: A scalar initial gradient norm was not a sufficient developmental predictor.

title: Tied-E continuation under A
result: Released tied-E states continued under A rather than E.
lesson: Matched starting states permit testing current training demands.

title: E→A release readout
result: A continuation contrasts.028/.045, held.662 versus E release.914.
lesson: Ongoing task differences mattered, not merely capacity to untie parameters.

title: Radial-gradient analysis
result: Gradient-direction summaries were mixed.
lesson: No reliable one-scalar acquisition law emerged from this diagnostic.

title: All focal pairs under F
result: F held pairs.961/.979/.982 versus A around.58 and H around.56.
lesson: The effect was not restricted to one privileged focal pair.

title: Exact F positive audit
result: F changed51,200/1,024,000 positive rows,5%.
lesson: The earlier claim that F changed only foils was incorrect and withdrawn.

title: Foil-only versus positive-only F
result: Foil-only held R.963, positive-only.453, fullF.989, A.487.
lesson: Positive-frequency shift was not necessary or sufficient under this construction; distractor repairs remain bundled.

title: Hardness/context control M
result: M held R.811 without the focal aligned hard comparisons; initial scalar loss/margin approximately matched.
lesson: Direct aligned comparisons were not necessary for any rescue; scalar hardness is not gradient matching.

title: Foil/positive/M trajectories
result: Foil-only amplified.956, positive-only compressed.052, M late partial.652.
lesson: Different learning paths accompanied similar scalar starting difficulty.

title: Quotient-collision audit
result: 51,214 collision rows,5%; merger raised F loss.00682→.0525 mostly on those rows.
lesson: The tested merger conflicts with part of the task; not a formal finite-render lower bound.

title: K collision versus L noncollision
result: Seed1701 held R K.975 versus L.795.
lesson: Collision-bearing examples were more effective in this comparison.

title: K/L second seed
result: Seed1702 held R K.925 versus L.558.
lesson: The direction survived a second discovery seed.

title: K/L acquisition trajectories
result: K consistently amplified earlier; L late behavior varied substantially.
lesson: The treatment effect did not identify a single necessary learning trajectory.

title: Acquisition figures
result: Rendered existing evidence into plots.
lesson: Visualization is a deliverable, not another scientific experiment.

title: Acquisition archive integrity
result: Verified archived file integrity/provenance.
lesson: Checks increase reproducibility, not replication count.

title: Merge/release assay
result: 256-update post hoc assay failed known L seed fork; K1702 weak, L gap.049<.10.
lesson: A superficially plausible acquisition predictor failed its own diagnostic cases.

title: Tied-start release with optimizer control
result: Train tiedL2k then release1k retained/reset moments; familiar gate passed but predicted seed fork failed.
lesson: Changing history can erase the phenomenon an assay claims to predict.

title: K/L fresh seed1703
result: All six frozen thresholds passed; K/L held R.866/.503 at2k, .932/.606 at8k; familiar near.999.
lesson: A bounded comparison-demand prediction succeeded on a new initialization.

title: Original L fork review
result: L1701 readout.372/.426/.875 at2/4/8k versus L1702.283/.268/.212; both distinguished earlier.
lesson: Late acquisition differences depend on history; the later fork's cause remained unresolved.
